# PsychSift

PsychSift is a private, local-first clinical knowledge-base interface for searching indexed source documents, reviewing evidence, and drafting source-backed clinical answers. It is a clinical reference prototype, not validated clinical decision support.

## What this is

PsychSift indexes private clinical reference documents (text, OCR, and image captions) into a vector database, then retrieves them to draft answers that cite back to the original source documents. It is local-first and private by design; when a generated answer cannot pass its quality gates it degrades to a source-only answer that still cites real documents rather than guessing. The product surface is 18 app modes sharing one search shell, and the routes below are the stable entry points.

## Key routes

- `/` opens the shared home. Add `?mode=<id>` to choose the workspace; mode ids include answer, documents, services, forms, differentials, dsm, specifiers, formulation, prescribing, tools, calculators, therapy-compass, factsheets, dictionary and sources.
- Bare mode paths such as `/services`, `/forms` and `/differentials` are compatibility redirects: unsubmitted they forward to `/?mode=<id>`; with `?q=...&run=1` they forward to that mode's own results surface (`/services/search`, `/forms/search`, `/differentials/search`).
- `/documents/search` opens the documents search results after submitting a documents-mode query.
- `/documents/:id` opens an indexed source document.
- `/sources/search` opens the ranked clinical source catalogue (`/sources` itself redirects to the shared home at `/?mode=sources`); `/sources/:sourceId` shows one source's identity, rating, locations and application usage.
- `/favourites` opens saved clinical work (requires a signed-in account).

**Authentication caveat:** Private indexed documents, source files, and clinical answer generation can require a signed-in session or local no-auth development mode. Public static files do not imply access to private source content.

## Agent orientation

These docs live in the repository, not on the served site — relative paths like `docs/codebase-index.md` resolve to `/docs/...` on the site and 404, so they are linked here as absolute GitHub URLs on `main`:

- [`docs/codebase-index.md`](https://github.com/BigSimmo/Database/blob/main/docs/codebase-index.md) — the deep map: module layout, APIs, Supabase, and the ingestion worker. Start here for any real code task.
- [`docs/site-map.md`](https://github.com/BigSimmo/Database/blob/main/docs/site-map.md) — the generated route index (regenerate with `npm run sitemap:update`).
- [`docs/agents-guide.md`](https://github.com/BigSimmo/Database/blob/main/docs/agents-guide.md) — agent onboarding, task navigation, and the tooling and documentation ownership map.
- [`docs/design-system/README.md`](https://github.com/BigSimmo/Database/blob/main/docs/design-system/README.md) — the design-system system of record; read before any UI work.

### Agent discovery

An AI agent may use these public, session-free entry points to orient itself:

- `/llms.txt` — this file.
- [`docs/codebase-index.md`](https://github.com/BigSimmo/Database/blob/main/docs/codebase-index.md) — module and architecture map.
- [`docs/site-map.md`](https://github.com/BigSimmo/Database/blob/main/docs/site-map.md) — generated route inventory.
- `/tools-guide.md` — an AI-facing tool guide published at the site root (added by a separate change).

## Clinical-content guidance

Treat generated answers as review aids. For clinical claims, rely on cited source evidence from the indexed library and verify source status, dates, and local governance before use.
